Original target timestamps: The main 2004--2021 experiment contains 18,410/3,945/3,945 raw training/validation/test timestamps and 18,404/3,939/3,939 forecast targets after six-snapshot windows are constructed separately within each partition. The target-time ranges (UTC) are 2 January 2004 12:00--7 August 2016 06:00 for training, 9 August 2016 00:00--20 April 2019 12:00 for validation, and 22 April 2019 06:00--31 December 2021 18:00 for testing. These are forecast target times, not input-window start times. The 1992--2003 extension is used only in the supplementary rolling-origin evaluation.
Retrospective rolling-origin design: We conducted a retrospective rolling-origin robustness evaluation using the extended 1992--2021 ERA5 archive. Expanding training periods were 1992--2007, 1992--2010, 1992--2013 and 1992--2016; their validation periods were 2008--2009, 2011--2012, 2014--2015 and 2017--2018, and their non-overlapping test periods were 2010--2012, 2013--2015, 2016--2018 and 2019--2021, respectively (F1--F4). F4$\prime$ instead trained on 2004--2016 and shared F4\textquotesingle s validation and test targets, isolating the addition of 1992--2003 training history within this protocol. The longest training history was 25 years; F1 and F2 used 16 and 19 years. Six models and five fixed seeds (42, 123, 7, 2024, 99) yielded 150 runs. The six models were XGBoost, Transformer, BiLSTM-Attention, BU-LSTM, BU-LSTM-Attention and Probabilistic BiLSTM-Attention; the plain BiLSTM control was not included.
Training history and conditional reliabi: On matched F4/F4$\prime$ test targets, extending training from 13 to 25 years reduced the six learning models\textquotesingle{} mean all-target RMSE by approximately 0.4--2.3\%. Upper-tail gains were not uniform, and seed-$t$ and test-sample bootstrap intervals did not always agree; both are retained. Conditional 95\% Gaussian coverage across F1--F4 was 0.953--0.963 overall, but only 0.801--0.828 for wet targets and 0.473--0.592 for upper-tail targets. Under the fixed Q95 rule, every learning model\textquotesingle s mean CSI was lower than Persistence in each period. The coverage and fixed-event diagnostics use fold-specific training Q95, whereas the history comparison uses the common original-main Q95 $=0.574048$~mm\,h$^{-1}$ for upper-tail targets. Fixed-cutoff event scores are distinct from the validation-selected decisions reported elsewhere.
Development-overlap and evaluation limit: The rolling-origin analysis is retrospective rather than a fully prospective or fully independent validation of model-design choices. The original training targets extended through 7 August 2016 and validation targets through 20 April 2019; these development data overlap the F1--F3 test years. F4 begins on 2 January 2019, so its early-2019 targets also overlap the original validation period; the original test targets begin only on 22 April 2019. The original test portion was not used for initial hyperparameter selection but had already informed the original model comparisons. Fold-specific fitting and preprocessing therefore do not remove development-stage overlap. Models were not retuned per fold; F1/F2 had only 16/19 training years. No ENSO-phase stratification, rolling plain-BiLSTM control or rolling Bernoulli--Gamma alternative was evaluated. Pooled bootstrap blocks can cross the 42-hour gaps between adjacent fold target sequences. These boundaries limit claims of temporal independence, attention-specific benefit and robustness to distributional formulation.
